title: Proactive Defense Benchmark against Deepfake Generation
claim: Defense methods rank very differently across pixel, perceptual and identity metrics, so no single method wins on every axis.
layout: Single hexagonal radar chart, five overlaid colored polygons, legend below
description: A single large hexagonal radar (spider) chart with six labeled axes: LPIPS, CIDR, BRISQUE, MSE, TE and ROB. Each axis has its own dashed concentric gridlines and numeric tick labels. Five semi-transparent filled polygons overlay one another, one for each defense: PGD in red, Disrupting in orange, DF-RAP in green, Anti-Forgery in blue and Latent Attack in purple. The orange polygon reaches far out on BRISQUE, TE and ROB. The red polygon spikes on LPIPS and MSE. The purple polygon spikes sharply on CIDR. The blue polygon stays small and central. A horizontal legend with colored line swatches sits at the bottom. The eye goes first to the large overlapping colored shapes and the sharp spikes, which show that each method peaks on different metrics.
caption: Performance of proactive defenses on SimSwap using multiple evaluation metrics. Additional results for other generators are provided in Appendix [ref].
abstract: Despite the proliferation of proactive defenses against deepfakes, the lack of a unified evaluation protocol precludes fair comparison and masks critical vulnerabilities. To bridge this gap, we present the first comprehensive benchmark that systematically assesses disruption, robustness, and transferability encompassing pixel, perceptual, and identity metrics. Our extensive analysis reveals that fidelity and identity metrics capture orthogonal performance axes, often leading to conflicting interpretations when relied upon individually. Furthermore, we identify a fundamental trade-off where peak white-box performance signals overfitting, and we introduce a calibrated evaluation to correct generator-induced identity bias. By exposing these blind spots, we establish a rigorous standard to guide the development of genuinely generalizable protections. Project page is available at: https://proactivedefensebenchmark.github.io/
